summary: New entry proposed from one occurrence. Input entry is absent; permitted glossary search maġram returned zero hits and entry ġrm returned no entry. No existing sense or stem is overwritten.

Only maġramno after gəd is directly attested. III is a provisional filing based on ma-ġram- against the usual II m-ġar- pattern; no unattested Preterit, full base-form pair or Detransitive is invented.

The Turoyo links broken ǧamat-mamat to aǧ ǧamat in the threatened response. This supports a financial-restitution domain independently of the machine English, but not an overt two-object frame: no him or l-marked liable person appears in the clause.

The adopted Ersatz verlangen reading remains provisional. Paying for/replacing the panes oneself is a possible direction-of-payment alternative to be checked; the English make him pay is not treated as proof of an omitted object.

Arabic ġrm financial vocabulary is a plausible comparison, not a demonstrated borrowing route or technical legal-fine history. No light-verb construction occurs: aǧ ǧamat is an ordinary affected-cost NP.

The quote is the supplied machine English, labelled as such. It is preserved rather than silently corrected to the competing payment reading; interpretation and the open alternative are stated separately.
Does maġramno here mean make the culprit pay/charge him, demand compensation, or pay for/replace the panes oneself? Please resolve direction of payment before removing the provisional gloss label.
What are the third-person Infectum and Preterit base forms, and is the loan filed asIII orII? Only1sg maġramno is attested.
Can a liable person be expressed as an object or l-complement, and how are the damaged thing, sum and beneficiary coded? No such complement is overt here.
